chapter: Guitarists and the Pierron and Brown bands
title: Happy Schilling's, Brown's and Fisher's bands; the all-night Brown party
summary: He liked Schilling's all-brass prize-fight band best. He recalls a Phi Delta Theta rush party where a white band, probably Tom Brown's, played until dawn and marched to the Chicago train.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: I've been asking about Fisher's band.

Because they overlap. Fisher was in Shilling's band and then they'd want to get another pickup band, they'd call it Fisher's band. But I think of the three that I liked Shilling's group the best because they featured, when they'd go into that prize fight, they had all brass except your clarinet. It was, I mean, right on down the line, carnet, trombone, clarinet, tuba, French horn, and never a string bass and they had drums. That was it. And boy, they were hell-bent for election. I have one memory, Bill, which I someday am going to try to track down by going up to the fraternity house and it's so clear in my mind and I've had arguments with people because the date is so clear. I was being rushed as a freshman into several fraternities at Tulane and this party was being given at the Phi Delta Theater House. They had hired this white band which I still am under the impression it was Tom Brown's band and it was in the spring of the year because that's when rushing goes on for the season, you see. And they had hired the band from nine until one and everybody liked it so much that they wouldn't go home so the fraternity boys chipped in again and hired them from one until three and they liked them so well that the dancers all chipped in and they kept them until six and they were leaving that morning for Chicago and they left the fraternity house on State Street near Claiborne and walked in the street playing music and me in the crowd until they put them on the train. Now that's a memory that's too big and too many people. I can't get anybody in Tom Brown's band to remember that.
